economics.simple_interest.title: Simple interest: future value and interest (F = P(1 + n·i))

economics.compound_interest.title: Compound interest: future value (F = P(1 + i)^n)
assumptions: Solving for P gives the present worth P = F/(1+i)^n.

economics.effective_rate.title: Effective annual interest rate from a nominal rate (i_eff = (1 + r/m)^m − 1)
assumptions: m = 12 monthly, 4 quarterly, 365 daily. As m → ∞ the effective rate approaches e^r − 1.

economics.annual_worth.title: Annual worth from a present amount (capital-recovery factor)
assumptions: At i = 0 the capital-recovery factor is the 0/0 limit A = P/n (principal spread over n periods).
method_references: A = P·i(1+i)^n/((1+i)^n − 1) (capital recovery); A = P/n at i = 0

economics.sinking_fund.title: Annual amount to accumulate a future sum (sinking-fund factor)
assumptions: At i = 0 the sinking-fund factor is the 0/0 limit A = F/n (no interest accrues).
method_references: A = F·i/((1+i)^n − 1) (sinking fund); A = F/n at i = 0

economics.irr.title: Internal rate of return from a cash-flow series (all real roots)

variables.name: cash_flows
variables.desc: cash flows [CF0, CF1, ...] (CF0 at t = 0; negative = outflow)

variables.name: irr
variables.desc: all real IRRs as decimals (rate > −1), ascending

assumptions: IRR solves NPV(r) = Σ CF_t/(1+r)^t = 0 for r > −1. All real roots are found from the NPV polynomial in x = 1 + r (including tangent/even-multiplicity roots and rates near −100 %); non-conventional flows (several sign changes) can therefore have several IRRs, all reported ascending.
method_references: Roots of NPV(r) = 0 via the NPV polynomial

economics.payback.title: Simple payback period (PP = C0/A)
assumptions: Ignores the time value of money; discounted payback is in cash_flow_series.

economics.benefit_cost_ratio.title: Benefit-cost ratio (B/C)
assumptions: B/C > 1 favours the project; benefits and costs are both present worths.

economics.depreciation_sl.title: Straight-line depreciation and book value
assumptions: k must not exceed the useful life n (a period beyond the life is rejected); at k = n the book value equals the salvage value.

economics.depreciation_db.title: Declining-balance depreciation and book value
assumptions: d = 2/n is double-declining balance. The book value is not floored at the salvage value (apply S as a floor in practice).

economics.depreciation_soyd.title: Sum-of-years-digits depreciation and book value
assumptions: k must not exceed the useful life n; at k = n the book value equals the salvage value.

economics.depreciation_table.title: Depreciation from a user-supplied percentage schedule (e.g. MACRS)

variables.name: rates
variables.desc: per-period percentages [r1, r2, ...] (MACRS rates are user inputs)

variables.name: book_values
variables.desc: book value at the end of each period

assumptions: Rates are entered as percentages and applied to the first cost P (MACRS convention, no salvage). No rate table is built in — the user supplies the percentages from the applicable code.

economics.break_even.title: Break-even point (quantity and revenue)
assumptions: Requires p > v for a positive break-even quantity.

economics.life_cycle_cost.title: Life-cycle cost: first cost plus present worth of uniform annual costs
assumptions: C_annual is a uniform end-of-period series discounted at rate i over n periods. At i = 0 the cost is simply C0 + n·C_annual.
method_references: LCC = C0 + C_annual·((1+i)^n − 1)/(i(1+i)^n); LCC = C0 + n·C_annual at i = 0

economics.cash_flow_series.title: Present/future/annual worth and discounted payback of a cash-flow series

variables.name: cash_flows
variables.desc: cash flows [CF0, CF1, ...] (CF0 at t = 0; negative = outflow)

variables.name: fw
variables.desc: future worth at the end of the last period

assumptions: Cash flows are end-of-period with CF0 at t = 0; n flows span an n − 1 period horizon. FW is compounded to the end of the last period; AW is the uniform series equivalent of the NPV over that n − 1 period horizon. Discounted payback is the first time the cumulative discounted flow reaches zero (interpolated within the crossing period); it errors if the project never pays back.
method_references: NPV = Σ CF_t/(1+i)^t; FW = NPV(1+i)^(n−1); AW = NPV·CRF; discounted payback

economics.modified_bc.title: Modified benefit-cost ratio ((B − O&M)/C)

variables.name: O
variables.desc: present worth of operating and maintenance costs

assumptions: Operating and maintenance costs are subtracted from benefits in the numerator and only the initial investment appears in the denominator (the modified B/C convention). A project is attractive when mbc > 1.

economics.continuous_compounding.title: Effective rate under continuous compounding (i_eff = e^r − 1)
assumptions: This is the m → ∞ limit of the nominal-rate formula i_eff = (1 + r/m)^m − 1.

source.derivation: Tangent (double) root: NPV·(1+r)² = (1+r)² − 2(1+r) + 1 = r² = 0 → IRR = 0 (even multiplicity; NPV touches zero without a sign change)
MACRS 5-year rates applied to P = 10000: 20 % → 2000, 32 % → 3200, …; book values subtract cumulatively to 0
i = 0 limit of the capital-recovery factor: A = P/n = 1000/3 = 333.333 (the 0/0 form i(1+i)^n/((1+i)^n−1) is replaced by its limit)
i = 0 limit of the sinking-fund factor: A = F/n = 1000/4 = 250
i = 0 limit: no discounting, LCC = C0 + n·C_annual = 100000 + 10·5000 = 150000
